 In 2016, The Godfather star Al Pacino’s former Beverly Hills rental, owned by Jackie Collins’ estate, was listed for $15.95 million after his nearly 18-year stay 
 In 2016, The Godfather star Al Pacino’s former Beverly Hills rental, owned by Jackie Collins’ estate, was listed for $15.95 million after his nearly 18-year stay 
 TOI Lifestyle Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Oct 20, 2026, 15:51 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print For nearly two decades, a house on Beverly Drive in Beverly Hills was home to Al Pacino, who rented the property from the estate of novelist Jackie Collins before continuing his tenancy under a new owner. The 1922-built residence, set behind mature trees and hedges in one of the city's established residential neighbourhoods, eventually became part of a much larger real estate transaction. Mansion Global reported that Collins had acquired the house alongside the neighbouring property in 1988. Years after she died in 2015, both homes came under the ownership of a real estate investor and his wife, who purchased them in separate transactions completed at the same time in 2016. By February 2025, Pacino's former rental was being offered for $15.95 million. Jackie Collins acquired the property in 1988
 British novelist Jackie Collins bought the Beverly Drive residence in 1988, along with the adjoining property, according to information provided by listing agent Bobby Syed of Coldwell Banker Realty. The house had a history within Collins's family before Pacino became its tenant. Syed said he understood that members of the family had lived there before the actor arranged to rent it. The property later became associated with Pacino's long stay in Beverly Hills, linking the novelist's former home to one of Hollywood's most recognisable actors. Pacino's tenancy lasted for approximately 18 years, extending beyond Collins's death in September 2015. He remained at the address after the property changed hands the following year, eventually leaving only a few months before the February 2025 listing. The property was rented and the later sale activity involved the owners who acquired the house after Collins's death. A new owner bought both Beverly Hills homes in 2016
 Real estate investor Ben Nehmadi and his wife, Bita Nehmadi, purchased the former Pacino rental for $9 million in 2016 through a limited liability company, according to records cited by Mansion Global. They acquired the neighbouring residence at the same time for $15.2 million. The two properties were separate assets, however, with their own valuations and subsequent listings. The larger neighbouring home was later offered for $59.5 million, while the house Pacino had occupied carried an asking price of $15.95 million in February 2025. The combined purchase is part of the property's financial history, rather than evidence that the actor had an ownership interest in either house. His connection to the smaller residence was through the long-running rental arrangement that began when Collins owned it. The 1922 residence sits on a substantial plot
 The house occupies a lot measuring approximately 0.69 acres in the Beverly Hills Flats. The residence itself covers around 5,200 square feet, with six bedrooms and six bathrooms. Although the surrounding properties sit relatively close together, established landscaping provides screening from neighbouring homes. Construction dates to 1922, but the building has undergone changes over the decades. A significant renovation took place in 1938 under architect Douglas Honnold, who later worked with John Lautner on the Beverly Hills Athletic Club in 1945. The residence therefore combines an older architectural history with more recent updates to its interiors. Some of its traditional character remains visible in the great room, where wood panelling and coffered ceilings give the space a period appearance. The room is divided into a family area with a fireplace and pool table, and an adjoining section containing a bar and room for a dining or card table. Other parts of the house have been modernised. A pool, cabana and full-size tennis court
 The grounds offer several amenities associated with larger Beverly Hills properties. Outside, there is a swimming pool, a hot tub and a cabana area, alongside a barbecue space with its own fireplace. A full-size tennis court is another feature of the property, one that Syed described as relatively uncommon in the Flats. Syed said that the city would permit a buyer interested primarily in the plot to pursue that option, indicating that the land accounted for much of the $15.95 million valuation. The listing agent pointed to its position between Rodeo Drive and the Beverly Hills Hotel, with both destinations within a short walk. The location places the property close to the city's luxury shopping and hospitality district while retaining its position on a residential street. Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports. The Times of India has not independently verified the property details, rental history or reported transaction values.
